title: Nonlinear refractive index of warm rubidium vapor
authors: L. Kardum, G. Premec, N. Šantić, D. Aumiler
abstract: The potential to precisely control both the linear and nonlinear index of refraction through optical manipulation of the atomic states has recently pushed warm alkali vapors to the forefront of research in the field of quantum sensors, quantum memories, and quantum fluids of light. Rubidium (Rb) vapor in centimeter-scale glass cells or millimeter-scale MEMS cells has proven to be a very promising platform for these applications, yet only a handful of research works have been dedicated to the investigation of the (non)linear refractive index of Rb vapor. We present results of theoretical calculations of the (non)linear refractive index of warm Rb vapor, based on the optical Bloch equations for 6-level Rb atoms interacting with a probe laser. They are compared to the experimental results obtained using an interferometric technique, showing excellent quantitative agreement. A Kerr nonlinear refractive index $n_2$ of up to $10^{-4}$ cm$^2$/W is obtained. Python scripts for all theoretical calculations presented in this work are provided, including the refractive index calculation, that can readily be used in practical implementations for simulating the (non)linear refractive index of Rb vapor including the effects of Doppler broadening, transit time broadening, pressure broadening, saturation, optical pumping, and spin-exchange collisions.
summary: This paper presents a comprehensive study determining the nonlinear refractive index of warm rubidium vapor by combining advanced theoretical modeling with precise interferometric measurements. The authors successfully modeled the complex atomic response using density matrix equations, achieving quantitative agreement with experimental data. This work is significant for quantum optics as it provides reliable parameters ($n_2$ and $I_s$) for designing optical devices utilizing alkali vapors.
main_problem: To theoretically calculate and experimentally measure the nonlinear refractive index of warm rubidium vapor.
main_result: The study achieved excellent quantitative agreement between theory and experiment, determining a Kerr nonlinear refractive index ($n_2$) up to $10^{-4} 	ext{ cm}^2/	ext{W}$. The results confirm that the nonlinearity is saturable.
method: Theoretical calculations utilize the optical Bloch equations solved via density matrix formalism, which are then compared against measurements taken using a Mach-Zehnder interferometer setup.
model_or_system: The system involves warm alkali vapors (specifically Rb) modeled by considering 6-level atoms interacting with a probe laser. The model incorporates complex broadening effects like Doppler, transit time, and pressure broadening.
key_observables: Nonlinear phase shift ($\delta\phi$), the nonlinear refractive index ($n_{NL}$), saturation intensity ($I_s$), and the Kerr coefficient ($n_2$).
important_parameters: Detuning from atomic resonance, laser power/intensity, and temperature (which dictates atom concentration).
main_assumptions: The model uses the rotating wave approximation and includes various collision broadening mechanisms while neglecting certain population transfer effects.
figures_summary: Figures compare simulated hyperfine absorption spectra to experimental data across varying temperatures; they also plot nonlinear phase versus detuning and versus laser power, demonstrating saturation behavior.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the theoretical framework using density matrix equations (optical Bloch equations) to applying this theory to simulate linear and nonlinear refractive indices. This is validated by comparing these simulations against detailed measurements obtained via interferometry.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly practical, quantitative tool for characterizing light-matter interaction in warm atomic media, which is crucial for developing quantum sensors and optical components based on alkali vapors.
